prompt:
Re-render image 1, the photograph, as a landscape photograph taken in a misty mountain forest with its identical camera: the same position, height, direction and lens, every the rocky peak and the hazy ridges, the wet path crossing the clearing, the pale rock pan and puddle in the near ground, the line of fir trunks on the right at the same place and size in the frame. The sun is low in the upper left, so shafts of light slant down to the right and shadows fall to the right and towards the camera. The path runs from the left edge across the clearing to the right. Nothing added to the misty mountain forest clearing, no pulling back, no mirror image.

Image 1 is the photograph with simple grey stand-ins drawn where each cast piece goes. Image 2 is the ancient tree. Image 3 is the wizard. Image 4 is the temple. The stand-ins show only where; the pieces show what.

The ancient tree in image 2, exactly that ancient tree, in the near foreground at the left edge, standing large and close to the camera, its roots on the moss at the bottom left and its limbs reaching right over the clearing, where image 1's stand-in outline is (x 0.00-0.28, y 0.00-0.84, about 84 percent of the frame height); keep its shape, colour and proportions, photographed in this light. The wizard in image 3, exactly that wizard, walking away from the camera on the wet path right of centre, towards the temple, whole and seen from behind, where image 1's stand-in outline is (x 0.55-0.63, y 0.36-0.70, about 34 percent of the frame height); keep its shape, colour and proportions, photographed in this light. The temple in image 4, exactly that temple, in the middle distance beyond the path, centre-right, standing on the open moss in front of the fir line, half veiled by mist, its base on the ground well behind the wizard, where image 1's stand-in outline is (x 0.53-0.68, y 0.20-0.47, about 27 percent of the frame height); keep its shape, colour and proportions, photographed in this light.

One frame, taken standing up at the edge of old forest, holds three distances at once that the field normally splits across three pictures. Near the boots is sharp wet moss on stone with one small true detail in it (refs 15, 17, 22). At the sides are dark, upright, moss-sided trunks that open a gap (refs 01, 05, 18). Through the gap, forested ridges step back, each paler and cooler than the last, until low cloud takes them (refs 19, 24). A few broad, soft bands of light slant down from the upper left through the mist between the trunks and the ridges (ref 14). The sun itself is never in the frame. If a picture loses the near stone, the ridges or the left-hand light, it could belong to anyone. With all three, it is ours.

Early morning after rain: low cloud in the valleys, mist hanging between the trees, the far ridges paling into haze, a soft low sun in the upper left sending shafts of light through the mist; still air, no people but the wizard.

Not the cathedral path, not the sun-burst, not the amber wash, not the overlook, not the white void, not the enchanted forest, not people and their buildings, not the lake mirror. No lettering except what this names.

Lock, repeated: the identical camera of image 1, sun upper left, path left to right, every the rocky peak and the hazy ridges, the wet path crossing the clearing, the pale rock pan and puddle in the near ground, the line of fir trunks on the right at the same place and size; the stand-ins become the pieces, nothing else is added to the misty mountain forest clearing.
